title: Bounded amplitude of open direct image on classical torsion sheaves
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $\Lambda$ be a finite ring with $\ell^r\Lambda=0$ for
some $r\ge1$, and let $j:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion of
finite-type $k$-schemes. Put $d=\operatorname{cd}(j)$ in the sense of
[def-kun-cd]. Then $d<\infty$, and:

1. for every sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$ and every
   $q>d$, $R^qj_{\mathrm{ét},*}F=0$;
2. for every such $F$ and every $q>d$,
   $\mathcal H^q\bigl(Rj_{\mathrm{proét},*}\nu_X^*F\bigr)=0$, where
   $\nu_X:X_{\mathrm{proét}}\to X_{\mathrm{ét}}$ is the comparison morphism;
3. consequently, if $M\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{ét}},\Lambda)$ has cohomology in
   degrees $[a,b]$, then $Rj_{\mathrm{proét},*}\nu_X^*M$ has cohomology in
   degrees $[a,b+d]$.

proof.text: Finite type over k gives CompactSpace X and locally Noetherian X and Y by Mathlib. The resulting quasi-separated spaces give QuasiCompact j and QuasiSeparated j. Apply torsionEtaleCohomologicalDimension_finite_of_finiteType. Unfold the defining infimum. Its set of finite bounds is nonempty, since otherwise the dimension is top, contradicting finiteness. Well-ordering of ENat gives csInf_mem, hence a natural d equal to cd(j) and the abelian torsion bound at d.

Define coefficientForget as sheafCompose of the ModuleCat-to-AddCommGrpCat forgetful functor. It is additive and faithful. Sectionwise finite limits and reflection by sheafToPresheaf give preservation of finite limits. For finite colimits, restriction of scalars along Z -> Lambda has a right adjoint (coextension); its composite with the ModuleCat Z / abelian-group equivalence is a left adjoint. The sheafification adjunction and sheafificationNatIso identify the induced composeAndSheafify with coefficientForget, proving preservation of finite colimits. All constructions use associative left modules, with no commutativity assumption.

proof.text: For an injective module-valued etale sheaf G, finiteCoefficientEtaleRealization is an equivalence onto modules over the constant ring sheaf O; its image I is injective. The sheafification counit identifies the underlying abelian sheaf of I with coefficientForget G. Injectivity passes to the module presheaf I.val. On every covering, injective_presheaf_module_cech_cocycle_lift_max in coefficient universe u+1 gives a primitive for each positive Cech cocycle. ShortComplex.ab_exact_iff gives exactness and zero homology. Transport through nonempty_etale_siteCech_complex_iso. Apply isZero_rightDerived_etale_of_cech_vanishing with every object and every cover; covers refine themselves by identities. Thus coefficientForget G is acyclic for abelian evaluation on every etale object.

proof.text: Underived direct image commutes definitionally with coefficientForget. The sheafified higher-direct-image description turns the preceding evaluation vanishing into direct-image acyclicity of forgotten module injectives: the section-cohomology presheaf is pointwise zero, hence so is its sheafification. The exact coefficient square therefore satisfies isIso_rightDerivedFunctorPlusBaseChange_of_rightAcyclic, giving the plus-derived coefficient comparison. This uses acyclicity, without asserting that the abelian forgetful functor preserves injectives.

Every module over the finite ring Lambda is additively torsion by IsAddTorsion.module_of_finite. Sheaf.IsTorsion.of_forall_isAddTorsion applies the abelian d-bound to coefficientForget F. The derived coefficient comparison, mapDerivedCategoryPlusHomologyFunctorIso and mapDerivedCategoryPlusSingleFunctor identify its zero cohomology with the forgotten module higher image. Faithfulness reflects zero by applying map_injective to its identity. This proves clause (1).

source.place: Clause (1), passage from torsion abelian sheaves to finite-ring modules.

proof.text: For any bounded-below module complex M, the canonical qcqs comparisonDirectImagePlus identifies pro-etale direct image of comparison pullback with comparison pullback of etale direct image. Install both exactness instances for comparisonUpperStar from siteComparison_finiteLevel, so mapDerivedCategoryPlusHomologyFunctorIso transports zero cohomology. Apply this to F[0] for clause (2), and retain the same transport for clause (3).

For clause (3), convert the two cohomological vanishing hypotheses into IsGE a and IsLE b in the ordinary derived category. Below a use the bounded-below right-derived functor lower-bound theorem directly. For the upper bound, identify its value on each sheaf with the ordinary derived functor by rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompatibility, giving IsLE d from clause (1). Transport CommShift and IsTriangulated along rightDerivedFunctorIsoKInjectives. The proved source-library DerivedCategory.isLE_obj_of_isLE is finite induction on truncation triangles: its pure-degree terms are cohomology sheaves placed in their degrees. Apply it to the bounded input to get IsLE (b+d), then transport back by rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompatibility. Finally apply the comparison of the preceding step. No spectral sequence or convergence theorem is required. The argument also covers a>b, since the input is then zero.
